clue.text: After electricity failure, stop eating meal at work

indicators.note: after tells us the eating words follow on behind the words about the electricity failure

blocks.note: electricity is power, as in a power supply
a break is a failure or breakdown in a supply
to fast is to stop eating

explanation.surface: After a power cut, someone gives up eating their working lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Failure here is a gap in supply, as in a cut; a power break is a British way of saying the lights went out.
explanation.definitionFit: A power breakfast is a business meeting held over the morning meal, so it is a meal eaten while working.

clue.text: Sales talk enthrals everybody in supermarket — bishop may deliver it

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the sales talk wraps around what follows
in places the word for everybody inside the word for supermarket

blocks.note: patter is a salesman's glib talk
a supermarket is a store
everybody is all

explanation.surface: A pushy salesman's pitch holds every shopper spellbound in the supermarket, and then a bishop turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the inner one is built first, then the sales talk splits around the whole of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral letter is an official message from a bishop to the clergy and congregations of the diocese.

clue.text: Chase little girl over piece of knitwear

definitions.note: woollen is used here as a noun, a garment made of wool

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the girl's name is read backwards

blocks.note: to woo is to chase romantically
Nell is a short form of the girl's name Helen or Eleanor

explanation.surface: Someone pursues a small girl about a jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Woollens are knitted garments made from wool, so a woollen can be a single item of knitwear such as a sweater.

clue.text: Half perused books, given another Kindle

indicators.note: half means only the first two of the four letters survive

blocks.note: perused means read
lit is short for literature, books in general

explanation.surface: Someone half-read some books and has been given a second Kindle e-reader.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital K disguises the verb kindle, to set alight, as Amazon's e-reader.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle is to set alight, so something given another kindling has been set on fire again.

clue.text: Biblical teaching by old Luther, for one

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces are simply placed side by side

blocks.note: RE is religious education, a school subject that teaches the Bible
former means old, of an earlier time

explanation.surface: Biblical teaching delivered by the old Martin Luther.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther was the German leader of the Protestant Reformation, a prime example of a religious reformer.

clue.text: Inattentive worker catching disease

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the worker surrounds the disease

blocks.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
BSE is mad cow disease

explanation.surface: A careless employee picks up an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent in mind is distracted and not paying attention, as in an absent look.

clue.text: Pretty lady travels round new fantastic location

indicators.note: the letters of lady move about, travelling into a new order
round means the jumbled lady goes around the letter for new

blocks.note: fair is an old word for pretty
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman journeys around some new, marvellous place.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairyland is the imaginary realm of fairies, a place that exists only in fantasy.

clue.text: Very late coming in, sees twitchy cat

indicators.note: coming in means the very late time is placed inside the other letters
twitchy means jumpy and restless, so the letters of sees jerk into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
one o'clock in the morning, 1 am, is very late at night, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Someone comes home in the small hours and sees a nervous cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 AM written with the numeral as the letter I gives IAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of domestic cat from Thailand, with pale fur and dark points.

clue.text: Turn up: no seats upstairs, so go back to where you were

definitions.text: go back to where you were

blocks.note: to turn up is to come
a theatre with no seats left is full
the circle is the upstairs seating in a theatre

explanation.surface: Someone arrives at a theatre, finds every upstairs seat taken, and heads home.
explanation.definitionFit: To come full circle is an idiom for returning to the starting point after a series of developments.

clue.text: Steals round place in underclothing

indicators.note: in places the round letter and the place abbreviation inside the underclothing

blocks.note: O is round in shape
PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses
a shift is a simple slip or chemise worn as underwear

explanation.surface: Someone pinches a round object and hides it in their undies.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoplift is to steal goods from a shop while pretending to be a customer.

clue.text: I paper over stage with wings

blocks.note: taken as written
a magazine, a mag, is a paper
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone papers over a theatre stage complete with its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: Wings look like the sides of a theatre stage, but these are an insect's.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the final, adult stage of an insect's life cycle, when it usually has developed wings.

clue.text: Maybe a little snowy in the breeding season?

definitions.text: Maybe a little snowy in the breeding season?

blocks.clueFragment: Maybe a little snowy in the breeding season?
blocks.note: surface reading: a bit of snow falling while animals breed in spring

blocks.clueFragment: Maybe a little snowy in the breeding season?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a small snowy owl, a youngster hatched in that season

explanation.walkthrough: Snowy reads as weather, but it is short for the snowy owl, and little means young.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, so a baby snowy owl is an example of one.

clue.text: Charter party once here beginning to embark on flowing sea

indicators.note: beginning to asks for only the opening letter of embark

blocks.note: runny means flowing, liquid
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
first letter of embark

explanation.surface: A chartered boat party sets out here onto a running sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Charter party sounds like a yacht hire, but it means the parties to Magna Carta, sealed at Runnymede by the Thames in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: King John and his barons met at Runnymede to agree Magna Carta, so the charter's participants were once gathered there.

clue.text: Prayer day that is coming round, at first chanted with a backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so chanted plus a is read in reverse
coming round means turning about, so that is is read backwards
at first puts the chanted piece at the front, before the day piece

blocks.note: chanted means sung
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A prayer for a day that is approaching, first sung with a choir behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei, Latin for Lamb of God, is a prayer said or sung in the Mass and other Christian liturgies.

clue.text: Order for soldiers mushy food, keeping men initially at attention

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the attention word surrounds the letter for men
initially asks for only the first letter of men

blocks.note: slop is unappetising semi-liquid food
someone who is at attention, listening hard, is all ears
first letter of men

explanation.surface: Soldiers standing to attention are served a bowl of mush.
explanation.walkthrough: At attention looks like the parade-ground position, which fits the surface, but it is read as listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Slope arms is a drill command telling soldiers to rest their rifles on the shoulder.

clue.text: Way to enter a university that is handed to you on a plate

definitions.text: handed to you on a plate

blocks.note: a gate is a way in
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A place at university is handed to someone without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Handed to you on a plate is an idiom for getting something easily, but here it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A gâteau is a rich cream cake, which is served to you on a plate quite literally.

clue.text: Region has area for one to entertain

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the area letter stands where the one letter was

blocks.note: a district is a region
A is the abbreviation for area
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A region has room for someone to throw a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To distract can mean to divert or amuse, taking someone's mind off their cares, which is to entertain them.

clue.text: Injury as limb at first sound twisted

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of limb
twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of limb
a noise is a sound

explanation.surface: An injury, as a limb that seemed healthy has been twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound looks like the adjective healthy, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is a wound or area of damaged tissue, a medical term for an injury.

clue.text: Sit with girl struggling to get skin cleaner

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sits with a girl who is struggling to get her skin clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A strigil was a curved metal scraper used in ancient Greece and Rome to remove oil and sweat from the body.

clue.text: Calming of gale is a bit of luck

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: a falling of the wind
second meaning: an unexpected gain

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into WIND and FALL, the wind falling as a gale calms.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is literally fruit blown down by wind, and figuratively an unexpected piece of good fortune.

clue.text: Delicious food not started — revolting excessive colouring

indicators.note: not started means the food word loses its opening letter
revolting means turning over, so excessive is read backwards

blocks.note: manna is the food from heaven, anything delicious
OTT is over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: A tasty dish that nobody has touched because of its revolting, overdone colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting looks like disgusting, which suits the food, but it means turning over.
explanation.definitionFit: Annatto is an orange-red dye made from seeds of a tropical tree, used to tint foods such as cheese.

clue.text: Success involves familiar wait

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include, so success holds the familiar word

blocks.note: a hit is a success
old means familiar, as in an old friend

explanation.surface: Success brings with it the usual waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hold it is a spoken command to stop and wait a moment.

clue.text: Reported for duty dressed, and dismissed

blocks.note: first meaning: arrived or assembled, as troops do
second meaning: attired, as in smartly dressed
third meaning: thrown out or expelled

explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate meanings of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned out means assembled for duty, dressed in a certain way, and expelled from somewhere.

clue.text: Members of kingdom are amusing Joe

blocks.note: fun means amusing
GI Joe is slang for an American soldier, a GI

explanation.surface: People in some kingdom find a man called Joe entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingdom sounds royal, but it is the biological kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungi form their own kingdom in biological classification, distinct from plants and animals.

clue.text: Comedy clubs having food brought round

indicators.note: the food is brought round, wrapping itself around the clubs letter

blocks.note: fare is food
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A comic scene at a club where food is served to the members.
explanation.definitionFit: A farce is a comic play built on absurd situations and slapstick.

clue.text: Cat losing head on European peak

indicators.note: losing head means the cat's first letter is dropped
on means placed after, so the cat piece follows the European letter

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat falls headfirst from a mountain top in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiger is a famous mountain peak in the Bernese Alps of Switzerland.

clue.text: Poor-sounding judge makes a mark

indicators.note: sounding means we go by how the words are spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: dire means very poor
a critic judges work

explanation.surface: A judge who sounds incompetent still makes his mark.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, dire critic and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic is an accent or other sign added to a letter, such as the cedilla or umlaut.

clue.text: In poverty, chose one bottle to get drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and confused, so these letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hard up picks a single bottle to get drunk on.
explanation.definitionFit: Living close to the bone means being hard up, with barely enough money to survive.
